tx_billiards_wall.blurb: A pocketed limestone bouldering wall on the cliff band above Belton Lake, the fourth big wall you meet when walking in from the gate at Rogers Park. Of the 27 problems here, most sit between V1 and V5, with a handful of much harder lines reaching V10, and several of the better ones top out high. Summer visits are comfortable because the face stays shady, and the nearby water offers a place to cool off afterwards. It suits a mixed group: warm-ups for newer boulderers, plus steep, powerful test pieces for strong ones.

tx_alpha_group.blurb: The nearest cluster of river-edge boulders when you wander downstream from Big Rocks Park near Glen Rose. It holds 26 problems that lean easy: roughly a third are V0 or below, plenty more fall at V1 and V2, and only a few climb past V3, topping out around V8. The setting is open, so the rocks catch sun for most of the day; early mornings and late evenings are the cooler windows. Other climbers are rarely around, which makes this a quiet spot for a relaxed session on beginner to intermediate problems.

tx_gus_fruh_boulder.blurb: Creekside limestone boulders in Austin's Barton Creek Greenbelt, on the west bank near the Gus Fruh sport wall. The 26 problems run from VB-level starts up to V9, with the bulk between V1 and V6 and a few hard lines above. The boulders stand roughly 20 to 25 feet tall, so expect taller problems and bring more than one pad. The climbing rewards footwork and body tension over raw strength. It feels quieter than the busier Austin crags, and cooler-weather mornings are the most pleasant time to visit.
tx_gus_fruh_boulder.parking_note: Leave the car on the street along Barton Hills Drive close to the Greenbelt access point at number 2642.
tx_gus_fruh_boulder.approach: From the Greenbelt Entrance sign, take the first right and follow the switchbacks down to the creek. Cross where the bed is dry or low, or use the rock dam upstream when the water is running.

tx_carnivore_boulders.blurb: A cluster of granite boulders on the southwest side of Little Dome at Enchanted Rock, close to the campground. The two biggest blocks carry steep, high-quality cracks, while smaller boulders nearby supply short top-rope laps and boulder problems. Of the 25 climbs here, most are trad leads from 5.7 up to 5.13, with bouldering from VB to about V5 and one aid line. Shade is easy to find and the walk-in is brief, so it is fairly popular for crack climbers, though Little Dome as a whole sees fewer people than the main dome.
tx_carnivore_boulders.approach: Take the Loop Trail from the campground area. After a short distance, turn right onto a narrow side trail that leads to the boulders.

tx_dragon_s_den.blurb: A busy bouldering section of East Mountain in Hueco Tanks, near El Paso, packed with problems for nearly every level. Of the 25 listed lines, a few are easy, a solid group lands in the V3 to V6 range, and an unusually deep set of V8 to V10 testpieces tops the grade spread. The area is known for some of the finest V5s in the park and a world-class V10. Terrain on East Mountain mixes roofs, walls and gullies, so the style varies from steep and powerful to technical face moves.

tx_lawless_wall.blurb: A small cove of pocketed limestone on the east bank of the Pecos River gorge, west of Del Rio, between the boat launch and the highway bridge. Most of the 24 climbs are bolted sport lines, with a couple of trad routes and a single boulder problem. The grade spread centers on 5.10, with a few easier lines and several in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. Walls here are vertical to slightly overhanging and more technical than typical Central Texas bouldery climbing. The cove stays shaded through the morning and into the afternoon, and some lines never see sun. Older bolts deserve judgment.

tx_centex_sportsman_cave.blurb: A horseshoe-shaped limestone cove on the shore of Lake Belton, west of Temple, with a massive roof and very steep climbing. Of the 24 climbs, most are sport routes in the 5.11 to 5.14 range, with the bulk at 5.12 and 5.13, plus a few boulder problems in a small cave you pass on the way in. The rock is gritty and can feel loose, improving higher on the wall. The cave is in shade all day, which helps in warm weather, and the lakeside setting is pleasant for a swim. Best for strong, experienced sport climbers.
